thread:
customer-ops: Getting a bunch of 429s from a customer using our API behind a corporate proxy. They say it only started after a deploy last night. Error looks like \"rate_limit_exceeded\".
maya: Can you paste a minimal repro and any request headers? Also which API key / org are they using?
customer-ops: Repro curl: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_prod_ABC123\" -H \"X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"input\": \"hi\"}'`
customer-ops: They appear to be NATing many clients through that one IP. Same API key across several internal teams.

jordan: Quick check of rate limiter logs for that IP shows spike at 2023-11-12T02:14Z: `ip=203.0.113.45 counts=1200/s 429s=980`.
jordan: But the auth logs also show the API key sk_prod_ABC123 belongs to org: org-777 with project: proj-ai-prod. Quota for org-777 is not exhausted in our ledger though.

maya: Huh. So IP is getting credited for the 429s in the limiter. Are we attributing to IP when multiple keys share same IP? That could be the proxy fallback behavior.

rate-limiter-bot: [info] request 3087654321.1 attr={auth:api_key, ip:203.0.113.45, org:org-777} decision=IP_RATE_LIMITER_HIT limit=1000/s window=1s counters={ip:1005, key:12}

alex: This looks like our heuristic that prefers IP attribution when ip counter >> key counter. With NATing, the IP counter wins and all tenants behind that IP get 429s even if key-level quotas are fine.

maya: Customer is impacted because they use a shared API key across teams behind the same corporate NAT. They expect per-key throttling, not per-IP.

customer-ops: Customer asked for a mitigation now, can we throttle by key only for their org?

jordan: Short term: we can flip a routing rule for org-777 to prefer key-level attribution. I can make a config change on the rate-limiter cluster. Would need restart of config rollout ~5m and a toggle back later.

maya: Please do that and confirm whether 429s stop. Also capture full request ids so we can correlate.

rate-limiter-bot: [action] applied policy override: org=org-777 prefer_key_attribution=true by=jordan id=rl-override-3098

jordan: Overrode now. Tell customer to retry.

customer-ops: Customer retried, reports errors went down to near zero. They see 200s for the same traffic patterns.

maya: OK short term fix validated. For long term we need to change the heuristic: prefer verified auth attribution when API key is present and fully authenticated. Fallback to IP only when auth is missing or anonymous.

alex: Agree. I'll open an engineering ticket to change the attribution precedence and add a test for NAT scenarios. Also propose adding a per-project quota header that proxies can set when they do per-team sharding. Rough plan: patch rate-limiter in next sprint, include migration flag and canary for 48h.

maya: Can we also add instrumentation that emits `attribution_source` in logs (values: key|ip|org|fallback) so incidents like this are easier to triage in future?

alex: Yep, will add that to the ticket.

jordan: Note: need to be careful about abuse: some customers deliberately IP-share to avoid per-key limits. New heuristic must respect abuse detection and retain IP-level backstops.

maya: I'll follow up with the customer about recommended best practice: use per-team API keys or enable our client-side connection pooling to avoid cross-team key reuse behind NAT. Also offered time-limited quota bump while they migrate.

customer-ops: Customer accepted temporary bump and will rotate their keys this week. They appreciated the quick patch.

maya: Marking this thread resolved pending engineering ticket: RL-1234.

alex: Ticket RL-1234: Change attribution precedence to prefer authenticated API key over IP when auth validates. Add attribution_source logs + tests. ETA: PR in 7d, canary in 14d.

customer-ops: Thanks everyone, closing on our side. :tada:
